rationale: bugs_open/059's read-time half. code_symbols is an indexed snapshot read by two correctness surfaces: the diagnosis code tier (diagnose_load_runtime's code_requests answers) and the council's code_checks tier (diagnose_code_lookup, including the prior_art seat's existence checks). Both render a header that SAYS 'treat a stale or empty answer as unknown, not absent' — but nothing COMPUTED staleness, so a reader had no fact to apply the rule with. The failure is proven, not hypothetical: the index sat 3 weeks stale (2026-07-02→2026-07-22, commit e3176f8) and every existence check in that window answered against old code; a code_request about any symbol added since returned empty, which reads identically to 'mechanism absent' — the exact false-negative the prior_art seat exists to catch, fed to it by its own tooling (the 019 family: a missing signal read as a negative one). The cadence half is fixed (scheduled task code-index-refresh, 24h, live 2026-07-24); this change is the read-time guard: every rendered answer now carries the index's own freshness — a quiet age+commit line when fresh, a loud STALE/EMPTY banner naming the age, the indexed commit and the remedy when not, and an unknown-freshness note (fail open) if the freshness query itself errors. Threshold 48h = one missed fire of the 24h cadence; deliberately a const, not step config (one platform-wide fact tied to that cadence row, and the banner always prints the ACTUAL age so a reader can judge regardless of the threshold). Change is committed (f21e54687), inert until the next image roll.

plan.summary: Add a shared freshness probe next to answerCodeCheck: codeIndexFreshness (one QueryRow per action run: newest code_symbols row's commit_sha + updated_at) feeding freshnessBanner, a pure decision/formatting function split out so every branch is unit-testable without a DB. Both render sites — diagnose_code_lookup's reviewer-answers header and diagnose_load_runtime's code-evidence header — prepend the banner. Falsification-tested branch by branch: fresh (quiet, names age+sha), stale (loud, names age/date/sha/remedy), boundary (age == threshold does not flag), empty index (loudest), query error (fail-open note, never silent).

edits.rationale: The probe and the pure banner. Lives in the file that owns answerCodeCheck — the shared answer path both consumers already use (reuse, not a new tier). Never fatal: an error degrades to an unknown-freshness note; the guard must not break the lookup it qualifies.
Render site 1 (the council tier, incl. prior_art's existence checks): prepend the banner to the header that states the rule.
edits.sketch:
b.WriteString("(an INDEXED snapshot — each answer names its commit_sha; treat a stale or\nempty answer as 'unknown', not 'absent'):\n")
+	// The read-time freshness guard (bugs_open/059): the header above SAYS to
+	// treat a stale answer as unknown, but until now nothing COMPUTED staleness,
+	// so a reader had no way to apply the rule. One query; loud when stale.
+	b.WriteString(codeIndexFreshness(ctx, params.DB))

edits.rationale: Render site 2 (the diagnosis gather): the verdict prompt's cite-or-abstain ACTS on absence, so the answer must carry its own freshness where the verdicter reads it.
edits.sketch:
cb.WriteString("(an INDEXED snapshot — each answer names its commit_sha; treat a stale or\nempty answer as 'unknown', NOT as 'absent'):\n")
+		// The read-time freshness guard (bugs_open/059): the line above states the
+		// rule; this line gives the verdicter the FACT needed to apply it. …
+		cb.WriteString(codeIndexFreshness(ctx, params.DB))

edits.rationale: Falsification tests: a guard whose job is to flag a fault must be SEEN flagging it. Every branch induced: fresh quiet, stale loud (names age/date/sha/remedy), boundary not-yet-stale, empty loudest, query-error fail-open.

plan.risks: 1) One extra QueryRow per action run (not per check) against code_symbols — negligible next to the per-check queries already run. 2) The banner adds ~1-3 lines to every code-answers section, spending a little bundle/context budget in every diagnosis and council round, including healthy ones — deliberate: provenance must be present precisely when nobody is suspicious. 3) The 48h threshold is a Go const coupled by comment to the 24h scheduled-task row; if the cadence interval is retuned the const does not follow automatically (mitigated: the banner always prints the actual age, so a reader can judge; and the STALE flag errs loud, not silent). 4) time.Now() inside codeIndexFreshness makes the DB-facing wrapper untestable for time — accepted, the decision logic is entirely in the pure freshnessBanner which takes now as a parameter. Reviewers should check: is header-level (once per section) the right granularity versus per-empty-result qualifiers (chosen: header-level — one fact, stated once, next to the rule it serves).
